title: Commodities Brief — 14 May 2026
intro:
Commodities Markets — Session Overview

Commodities remain range-bound within the broader supercycle framework as dollar strength weighs on precious metals while agricultural markets surge on weather concerns. Risk sentiment stays cautiously optimistic despite ongoing geopolitical headwinds.

sections.heading: Precious Metals
sections.content: Gold trades sideways at $4705.80/oz, consolidating recent gains as real rates stabilize and central bank demand provides underlying support. Silver underperforms at $87.54/oz (-1.52% intraday) on industrial demand concerns. Platinum weakens to $2142.10/oz amid automotive sector headwinds, while palladium holds $1516.00/oz. Copper retreats to $6.58/lb, signaling near-term growth uncertainty despite constructive medium-term fundamentals.

sections.heading: Energy
sections.content: Oil markets maintain strength with WTI at $101.09/bbl and Brent at $105.79/bbl, supported by tight global inventories and robust summer driving season expectations. The $4.70/bbl Brent-WTI spread reflects persistent midstream bottlenecks. Natural gas finds footing at $2.88/MMBtu on cooling demand forecasts.

sections.heading: Agriculture
sections.content: Grain complex rallies sharply on adverse weather patterns across key growing regions. Wheatsurges to $678.25/bu (+9.00% weekly) on European drought concerns and Black Sea export disruptions. Corn climbs to $478.50/bu on planting delays, while soybeans hold steady at $1217.25/bu.

sections.heading: Trade Ideas
sections.content:
LONG: Wheat (weather premium expanding), WTI crude (inventory drawdowns), Gold (CB buying intact)
SHORT/HEDGE: Silver (industrial demand lag), Natural gas (oversupplied market)

sections.heading: Key Risks
sections.content: Dollar breakout above 108 DXY could pressure metals complex. Sudden weather normalization threatens grain rally sustainability. OPEC+ production discipline remains uncertain ahead of June meeting.
